cards.name: Reticulation
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Sketch filter that imitates the controlled shrinking and cracking of film emulsion: the image is rebuilt from clumped, irregular grain in the Foreground and Background swatch colours (black and white by default), dense and dark in the shadows and lightly speckled in the highlights. The original colours are replaced by the two swatches.
use_for: gritty darkroom / aged-film texture on a black-and-white poster photo
turning a soft or low-quality video still into a deliberate grainy graphic so the softness reads as style
two-colour grain treatment in brand colours (set the swatches first) for a zine or gig flyer
grainy texture layer blended in Multiply or Overlay over the colour original
avoid: keeping the photo's colours: everything is remapped to the two swatches; for coloured grain use Filter/Noise/Add Noise or Filter/Artistic/Film Grain
unpredictable colours: the result uses the current Foreground / Background swatches, so reset them to black / white or set them in the script before running
small type and thin lines (the white 'PGD 2026' and hairlines on the plate): the grain clumps break them up

not listed in the Filter menu by default in Photoshop 2026 (harvest: menu_visible false): open it from Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch, or tick 'Show all Filter Gallery groups and names' in Preferences > Plugins; scripts reach it directly with executeAction
CMYK or Lab documents: Filter Gallery effects run only on Grayscale / RGB (harvest supported_modes); 16/32-bit documents also block the Filter Gallery (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed)

params.does: how densely the grain clumps are packed; higher gives a heavier, more obvious grain
params.typical: 0-50; 12 harvest default, 25-40 for a strong texture

params.name: Foreground Level
params.does: weight of the Foreground (dark) colour: raising it pushes more of the image into the dark grain
params.typical: 0-50; 40 harvest default, 25-35 to keep mid-tones readable

params.name: Background Level
params.does: weight of the Background (light) colour: raising it keeps more of the light areas clean
params.typical: 0-50; 5 harvest default, 5-15

pairs_with: Image/Adjustments/Levels or Curves before it (more contrast gives cleaner clumping on a soft photo)
blending the result in Multiply / Overlay over a colour copy to bring colour back
Filter/Convert for Smart Filters (keeps the settings editable and fadeable)

cards.name: Stamp
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Sketch filter that simplifies the image into flat, smoothed two-tone shapes in the Foreground and Background swatch colours, as if printed with a rubber or wood stamp. clean black-and-white base to trace into a vector logo or stencil
stencil / screen-print look for merchandise mock-ups
avoid: low-contrast or soft subjects whose tones sit close together: they fall to one side of the split and merge into one blob; raise contrast with Levels / Curves first
fine detail and small type: Smoothness rounds counters and thin strokes away
unpredictable colours: it uses the current Foreground / Background swatches; reset them to black / white or set them in the script
a plain threshold without smoothing: Image/Adjustments/Threshold gives hard pixel-exact black and white

cards.name: Torn Edges
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Sketch filter that rebuilds the image as two-tone areas in the Foreground and Background swatch colours whose borders are ragged and fibrous, as if the shapes were torn out of paper. avoid: keeping colour: everything becomes the two swatch colours; for a coloured torn edge, mask the colour photo with a Torn Edges result
soft, low-contrast photos: subjects merge into one mass with no visible tear; add contrast with Levels / Curves first
unpredictable colours: it uses the current Foreground / Background swatches; reset them to black / white or set them in the script

cards.name: Water Paper

cards.name: Diffuse
cards.summary: Shuffles pixels a short random distance to soften focus, giving edges a speckled, frosted-glass fringe: Normal moves pixels randomly, Darken Only lets only darker pixels spread, Lighten Only only lighter ones, and Anisotropic moves pixels along the direction of least colour change, which smooths tones into a soft painterly look. There is no strength control, so on a large image the change is fine-grained and shows mostly along hard edges.
use_for: frosted-glass or dithered edge on hard graphics and type
faux painting: Anisotropic mode, repeated a few times, smooths a photo into soft brush-like tones
breaking up hard pixel edges or banding before another stylize filter
Darken Only / Lighten Only to thin or thicken light details with a speckled edge
avoid: a visible soft-focus blur on a big, already soft photo: the shift is only a pixel or two (general knowledge, not measured here), so the 1920 px plate's photo barely changes; use Filter/Blur/Gaussian Blur or run Diffuse on a smaller copy
a fixed amount: there is no amount or radius setting; re-run the filter (Filter/Last Filter) to build it up
the 'Lighten Only' option is sent as the enum value 'lightOmni' (harvest), not 'lightenOnly'

params.name: Mode
params.does: how pixels move: normal = random scatter; darken only = only darker pixels spread; lighten only = only lighter pixels spread; anisotropic = smooth along tones
params.typical: normal for a dithered edge; anisotropic for a painterly smoothing

pairs_with: Image/Image Size down then back up around it (makes the scatter coarser and visible)
Filter/Stylize/Emboss or Find Edges afterwards (textured, rough-edged outlines)
Edit/Fade Diffuse straight after (lowers its strength)

cards.name: Emboss
cards.summary: Makes the image look raised or stamped into a surface: flat areas turn mid-grey and each edge is drawn as a light ridge on one side and a dark ridge on the other, lit from the Angle, with a little of the original colour left along the edges. Height sets how far the relief is offset and Amount how strong (and how colourful) the edges are.
use_for: embossed metal, stone or paper relief look for a logo, coin or plaque mock-up
grey relief map to blend in Overlay / Hard Light over the photo for a carved texture
bas-relief poster backgrounds from a photo
grey height / bump map to export for a texture or 3D app (Lighting Effects and 3D are not in the Photoshop 27.4 harvest)

soft, low-contrast photos at the default Height 3 / Amount 100: edges are weak and the relief barely shows; raise Height and Amount

reading the scripted values back: the harvest's probes (even angle / height / amount = 1) all reported 135 / 3 / 100 because the result descriptor executeAction returns is not a read-back for this filter: it reports the dialog's last-used values (proven in the PS effect gallery: re-applying the reported values gives different pixels, the values sent reproduce the frame exactly), so judge a scripted run by its pixels; the gallery frame at 8 / 300 confirms sent values are applied. params.name: Amount

the embossed copy in Overlay / Hard Light over the original (carved texture that keeps colour)

cards.name: Extrude
cards.summary: Breaks the image into a grid of square blocks or four-sided pyramids that seem to project out of the screen toward the viewer, giving a 3D tiled texture with shaded sides. Size sets the base of each block, Depth how far the tallest ones stick out, and Random / Level-based decides whether depth is random or follows brightness (bright areas protrude more); Solid Front Faces fills each block's front with its average colour instead of the image.
use_for: 3D block / pixel-tower background for tech, data or gaming graphics
abstract pyramid-stud texture from a photo for a poster backdrop
transition-style 'exploding tiles' still for a video thumbnail
retro 90s 3D effect on a bold graphic
avoid: subjects that must stay recognisable: faces and type are cut into blocks with perspective sides; apply it to a background layer or mask it
small Size on a large image: blocks become tiny and the result reads as noise; on a 1920 px image use 30-60 px
a flat mosaic without 3D sides: use Filter/Pixelate/Mosaic
the 'Blocks' type is sent as the enum value 'blacks' (harvest), not 'blocks'

params.name: Type
params.does: shape of each element: Blocks (square front face and four sides) or Pyramids (four triangular sides meeting in a point)
params.typical: Blocks for a mosaic-tower look, Pyramids for a studded texture

params.name: Size
params.does: length of each block's or pyramid's base side in pixels
params.typical: 2-255; 30 harvest default, 30-60 on a 1920 px image

params.name: Depth
params.does: how far the tallest elements extend toward the viewer
params.typical: 1-255; 30 harvest default, 40-90 for strong 3D

params.name: Random
params.does: Random gives each element an arbitrary depth; Level-based makes depth follow brightness so light areas stick out most
params.typical: Level-based keeps the image's shapes readable; Random for chaotic texture

params.name: Solid Front Faces
params.does: fills each block's front face with its average colour instead of the image (Blocks only)
params.typical: on for a clean mosaic-tower look, off to keep the picture on the faces

params.name: Mask Incomplete Blocks
params.does: hides blocks that would project beyond the selection or canvas edge
params.typical: off, on for a tidy edge

pairs_with: Image/Adjustments/Curves afterwards (more contrast between the lit and shaded block sides)
a layer mask to keep the subject or headline area flat
Image/Adjustments/Hue/Saturation to push the tiles into brand colours

cards.name: Oil Paint
cards.summary: Repaints the image as thick oil paint: tones are swept into directional brush strokes, and with lighting on the strokes get raised impasto ridges with highlights lit from a chosen angle. Stylization sets the stroke style (daubed to smooth, swept), Cleanliness the stroke length, Scale the paint thickness, Bristle Detail the bristle grooves and Shine the gloss of the ridges.
use_for: painted-portrait or fine-art poster look from a photo
hiding the softness and compression of a video still under a painterly finish
storybook / illustrated backgrounds behind headline type
brush-stroke texture layer blended over a photo at low opacity
avoid: small images or tiny Scale on a big image: strokes are too fine to read; on a 1920 px image raise Scale and Stylization
faces in close-up at high Stylization: features swirl into abstraction; mask the face or lower the values
a graphics processor switched off: the harvest notes Oil Paint is GPU-dependent; that it is greyed out without Preferences > Performance > Use Graphics Processor is general knowledge, not checked

script key names: the harvest read back brushScale (dialog Scale), microBrush (Bristle Detail), lightDirection (Angle) and specularity (Shine), while the terminology declares scale / bristleDetail / angularDirection / shine; the range probe was inconclusive because the result descriptor executeAction returns is not a read-back for this filter: it reports the dialog's last-used values (proven in the PS effect gallery: re-applying the reported values gives different pixels, the values sent reproduce the frame exactly), so judge a scripted run by its pixels, so stay inside the dialog ranges and check the render
the mapping of brushScale / microBrush / lightDirection / specularity to the dialog sliders is inferred from their names and defaults, not confirmed by the harvest
scripted Smart Filter workflows: applying it to a Smart Object failed in the harvest (see non_destructive); apply it to a pixel layer

params.name: Stylization
params.does: stroke style: low values give a daubed look, high values smooth, long swept strokes
params.typical: 4 harvest default; 6-10 for an obvious painted look (dialog range about 0.1-10, general knowledge, not harvested)

params.name: Cleanliness
params.does: stroke length and smoothness: low gives short, choppy, textured strokes, high long and clean ones
params.typical: 2.3 harvest default; 4-8 (dialog range about 0-10, general knowledge, not harvested)

params.name: brushScale
params.does: paint thickness (dialog Scale): low gives a thin coat, high thick paint with bigger, more visible raised strokes
params.typical: 0.8 harvest default; 3-8 on a 1920 px image (dialog range about 0.1-10, general knowledge, not harvested)

params.name: microBrush
params.does: bristle detail (dialog Bristle Detail): how strongly individual bristle grooves show inside each stroke
params.typical: 10 harvest default; 4-10 (dialog range about 0-10, general knowledge, not harvested)

params.name: lightingOn
params.does: turns the impasto lighting on or off; off gives flat strokes with no raised ridges
params.typical: true for thick paint, false for a flat painted look

params.name: lightDirection
params.does: angle the light comes from (dialog Angle), which sets where the stroke ridges catch highlights
params.typical: -60 harvest default; change it to move where the ridges catch the light

params.name: specularity
params.does: shine of the paint surface (dialog Shine): higher gives glossier, more pronounced ridges
params.typical: 1.3 harvest default; 2-4 for strong relief (dialog range about 0-10, general knowledge, not harvested)

pairs_with: a duplicate of the photo layer (blend or mask the painted copy; Smart Filter apply failed in the harvest)
Image/Adjustments/Vibrance or Curves after it (richer paint colours)
Filter/Texture/Texturizer Canvas (painted-on-canvas surface)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putBoolean(stringIDToTypeID("lightingOn"), true); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("stylization"), 8); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("cleanliness"), 5); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("brushScale"), 5); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("microBrush"), 6); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("lightDirection"), -60); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("specularity"), 3); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("oilPaint"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // keys and types as read back by the harvest; keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
